title: Introduction to MaxMin
text: Gonzalez (1985) algorithm builds selection greedily: start seed point, repeatedly add whichever unselected point farthest current selection. greedy rule guarantees 2-approximation optimal Tk runs O(N · m) time. default Gonzalez() runs ensemble cheap O(N) seeding strategies — "centroid", "peripheral", three "random_furthest" starts — returns whichever pass produced highest Tk (best--five selection). "centroid" seed computed coordinates, distance matrix eurodist dropped remaining seeds apply. random starts pivot points drawn session RNG, set seed (set.seed()) reproducible selection. Pass pivots vector () random starts — length sets number starts, integer(0) disables ; pass character vector seed choose custom ensemble, single name one strategy. can also request specific seeding strategy custom ensemble subset: pairwise distances objects known — coordinates work — computing storing N×N distances expensive (e.g. large phylogenetic trees, tree--tree distance requires calculation), pass Gonzalez() function place distance matrix. function takes one index returns distances object N objects — one column matrix. Gonzalez calls n times, full N×N matrix never built; must supply N (number objects), since read function. (column simply indexes matrix already , keep example self-contained; point col_of instead compute column trees, sequences, metric coordinate embedding.) integer seed (fixed start index) default peripheral seed available path — richer ensemble anchors need whole matrix.
code: set.seed(1) idx_ens <- Gonzalez(eurodist, n = 6L)   # default: best-of-five O(N) seeds  # Which seeding strategy won? attr(idx_ens, "winning_strategy") #> [1] "peripheral"       "random_furthest1" "random_furthest2" "random_furthest3" idx_diam <- Gonzalez(eurodist, n = 6L, seed = "diameter") TkScore(eurodist, idx_diam) #> [1] 1014  idx_anti <- Gonzalez(eurodist, n = 6L, seed = "anti_medoid") TkScore(eurodist, idx_anti) #> [1] 1014 dm <- as.matrix(eurodist) col_of <- function(i) dm[, i]       # one column on demand Gonzalez(col_of, n = 6L, N = nrow(dm), seed = 1L) #> [1]  1 12 20 16  5  2

title: Introduction to MaxMin
text: DropAdd heuristic (Porumbel, Hao & Glover 2011) refines initial selection alternating drop add moves guided FIFO tabu list prevents short cycles. fully deterministic reproducible, typically reaches ≈ 99 % optimal Tk. max_no_improve main stopping knob: algorithm terminates many consecutive iterations without improvement Tk. coordinate data N large enough make distance matrix infeasible (roughly N > 46 000), use DropAddTSPoints(), accepts coordinate matrix directly.
code: res_da <- DropAddTS(eurodist, m = 6L, max_no_improve = 500L)  labels(eurodist)[res_da$indices] #> [1] "Athens"    "Barcelona" "Cherbourg" "Lisbon"    "Stockholm" "Vienna" res_da$objective     # T_k achieved #> [1] 1294 res_da$iters         # iterations completed #> [1] 516 res_da$time_s        # wall-clock seconds #> [1] 0.0001935959

title: Introduction to MaxMin
text: GRASP + path relinking (Resende et al. 2010) combines randomised greedy construction phase extended local search refines elite set good solutions interpolating elite-pair trajectories (path relinking). achieves highest Tk three heuristics, proportionally higher cost. construction phase stochastic, always set seed reproducibility: max_no_improve controls many consecutive non-improving GRASP iterations trigger termination; time_budget_s available absolute time cap interactive batch use.
code: res_gr <- GraspPR(eurodist, m = 6L, max_no_improve = 50L, seed = 42L)  labels(eurodist)[res_gr$indices] #> [1] "Athens"    "Barcelona" "Calais"    "Lisbon"    "Stockholm" "Vienna" res_gr$objective #> [1] 1305 res_gr$pr_calls   # path-relinking calls performed #> [1] 90

what: Comparing methods on a simulated example
title: Introduction to MaxMin
text: see methods relate visually, generate 50 points two dimensions select m = 8 . Even small difference Tk can correspond meaningfully dispersed selection. Plotting selections point cloud makes differences concrete. two methods select index, symbols overlap; Tk table captures quality distinction even visual overlap high.  Selections returned method 50 random 2-D points (m = 8). Coloured symbols mark selected points; grey circles full candidate set. small jitter separates symbols shared indices.
code: set.seed(42) pts <- matrix(rnorm(100), ncol = 2)   # 50 points, 2 dimensions d50 <- dist(pts) m   <- 8L idx_gonz <- Gonzalez(d50, n = m) res_da50 <- DropAddTS(d50, m = m, max_no_improve = 500L) res_gr50 <- GraspPR(d50, m = m, max_no_improve = 50L, seed = 42L) scores <- c(   Gonzalez  = TkScore(d50, idx_gonz),   DropAddTS = res_da50$objective,   GraspPR   = res_gr50$objective ) round(scores, 3) #>  Gonzalez DropAddTS   GraspPR  #>     1.416     1.428     1.428 methods <- list(   Gonzalez  = idx_gonz,   DropAddTS = res_da50$indices,   GraspPR   = res_gr50$indices ) cols <- c(Gonzalez = "#E41A1C", DropAddTS = "#377EB8", GraspPR = "#4DAF4A") pchs <- c(Gonzalez = 24L, DropAddTS = 21L, GraspPR = 22L) # Small per-method shift so coincident selections remain distinguishable dx   <- c(Gonzalez = 0, DropAddTS =  0.04, GraspPR = -0.04) dy   <- c(Gonzalez = 0, DropAddTS = -0.04, GraspPR =  0.04)  plot(pts, pch = 1L, col = "grey75", asp = 1L,      xlab = "x", ylab = "y",      main = "MaxMin method comparison")  for (nm in names(methods)) {   sel <- methods[[nm]]   points(     pts[sel, 1L] + dx[nm],     pts[sel, 2L] + dy[nm],     pch = pchs[nm], col = cols[nm], bg = cols[nm], cex = 1.6   ) }  legend("topright",        legend = paste0(names(methods), "  (Tₖ = ", round(scores, 3), ")"),        pch = pchs, col = cols, pt.bg = cols, pt.cex = 1.4, bty = "n")

title: Introduction to MaxMin
text: small instances (roughly N ≤ 25–30), ExactMaxMin() solves problem proven optimality via node-packing integer programme (Sayyady & Fathi 2016), using highs solver. $proven = TRUE certifies selection can achieve higher Tk. ExactMaxMin() NP-hard; instances ~30 candidates require time budget tackled heuristics .
code: set.seed(1L) pts30 <- matrix(rnorm(60L), ncol = 2L) d30   <- dist(pts30) res_ex <- ExactMaxMin(d30, m = 6L, time_budget_s = 30L)  res_ex$proven      # TRUE  ⟹  objective is the global optimum #> [1] TRUE res_ex$objective #> [1] 1.616311  # Compare to the greedy heuristic on the same instance res_gonz30 <- Gonzalez(d30, n = 6L) c(exact    = res_ex$objective,   Gonzalez = TkScore(d30, res_gonz30)) #>    exact Gonzalez  #> 1.616311 1.616311

title: DropAdd Tabu Search for the Max-Min Diversity Problem — DropAddTS
text: MMDPo objective optimised $$\min_{x,y \X} d(x,y) + \epsilon \sum_{x,y \X} d(x,y),$$ \(\epsilon = 10^{-9}\), pairwise sum acts tie-break. Tabu mechanics. algorithm maintains integer iter stamp every point, set iteration point last entered left selected set \(X\). main-loop iteration point smallest iter value (oldest member, FIFO) dropped, point \(Z \setminus X\) maximising lexicographically \((\mathrm{min\_dist}, \mathrm{sum\_dist})\) added. FIFO invariant guarantees across window \(m\) iterations every initially-selected point dropped exactly re-eviction.

title: Deterministic Gonzalez furthest-point selection — Gonzalez
text: Greedy k-centre selection (Gonzalez 1985). Iteratively selects point furthest current selection, 2-approximation k-centre problem. quality result depends first (seed) point; default Gonzalez() runs ensemble cheap O(N) seeding strategies keeps selection largest minimum pairwise distance (TkScore()). default ensemble two deterministic O(N) seeds "centroid" "peripheral" together three "random_furthest" starts – best--five selection. random starts use session RNG, set seed (set.seed()) reproducible selection. "centroid" seed computed coordinates, distance matrix default drops keeps "peripheral" plus random starts. Costlier O(N^2) anchors ("diameter", "anti_medoid", "medoid", "rowsum", "rownorm") available opt-seed strategies.

Default 100. max_iter Optional integer hard cap GRASP refinement iterations (excluding elite-set construction). NULL (default) leaves max_no_improve sole control. elite_size Size elite set |ES|. Default 10. alpha RCL threshold; alpha = 1 pure greedy, alpha = 0 uniform random. Default 0.8. time_budget_s Optional wall-clock ceiling seconds. Default Inf (ceiling, fully reproducible). finite value caps runtime makes result machine-dependent. seed Optional integer; supplied, set.seed(seed) called entry. title: Peripheral seed index for Gonzalez farthest-first selection — MaxMinSeed
text: Anchors: "centroid" point farthest coordinate mean (argmax ||x - x_bar||), O(N * dim) approximate diameter endpoint. Computed coordinates, requires points; unavailable distance-matrix path, "peripheral" serves role. "peripheral" Two sweeps: point furthest point 1, point furthest (diameter-endpoint approximation), O(N). anchor reachable distance-column oracle (function path Gonzalez()). "random_furthest" point furthest random pivot, O(N). pivot drawn session RNG; set seed (set.seed()) reproducible index. "diameter" row endpoint diameter pair (maximum pairwise distance). Degenerate data (d_max <= 0) falls back 1. "anti_medoid" point furthest 1-median (medoid). "medoid" 1-median , .min(rowSums(d)). "rowsum" point maximising sum distances others (1-anti-median). "rownorm" point maximising sqrt(sum d^2), L2 counterpart "rowsum".

title: Local-search polish for a max-min diversity selection — PolishSelection

T_k -n_critical monotone non-decreasing across accepted swaps, iteration terminates without tabu list. intended use post-step greedy max-min selector — example Gonzalez(). Calling PolishSelection() 1-swap local optimum -op.

title: MaxMin 0.0.0.9000 (development)
text: Initial release: tiered toolbox Max-Min Diversity Problem (MMDP / discrete p-dispersion), extracted FurthestPoint study package can depended CRAN packages (e.g. TreeSearch). Gonzalez(): deterministic farthest-first selection distance matrix, Euclidean coordinates (points =), -demand distance-column oracle (pass column function d, N =) spaces coordinate embedding. default seed runs best--five ensemble cheap O(N) seeds — "centroid", "peripheral", three "random_furthest" starts (whose pivots drawn session RNG; set seed reproducible selection, supply via pivots argument) — keeps best TkScore(). Costlier O(N²) anchors ("diameter", "anti_medoid", "medoid", "rowsum", "rownorm") available opt-strategies. DropAddTS() / DropAddTSPoints(): DropAdd tabu search (Porumbel et al. 2011), matrix matrix-free coordinate paths. ExactMaxMin(): exact node-packing optimum (Sayyady & Fathi 2016) via highs MILP backend. GraspPR(): GRASP path relinking (Resende et al. 2010), dense-matrix-refinement metaheuristic attains highest T_k package’s methods small medium instances. PolishSelection(): critical-edge-anchored 1-swap local search. TkScore(): k-centre objective (minimum pairwise distance). MaxMinSeed(): exposes peripheral seed indices directly.
